title: Refactor anchor constraints and establish publish-curator workflow for UI library
creator: Rafael Gómez
description: Background: Our Figma library has accumulated several inconsistent anchor/constraint patterns across data controls (buttons, tables, charts). This causes fragile auto-layout behavior when instances are nested or when responsive density changes are applied. The goal for this ticket is twofold: 1) normalize anchor/constraint primitives to a small, documented set (HorizontalAnchor / VerticalAnchor / Stretch) and migrate components to use the new primitives; 2) introduce a lightweight "publish-curator" workflow and checklist so library publishes are gated by a repeatable QA on anchors, token mappings, and instance resiliency.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document the canonical anchor primitives and mapping guidance in the design confluence page (Design System > Anchors)
All primary button, compact button, table row, and chart legend components use the new anchor primitives and pass the auto-layout stress checks (see QA steps)
A publish-curator checklist exists in Drive and is used to validate each major library release; at least one release has been gated using this checklist
A Figma inspection plugin run (script) is available which flags components that still use deprecated constraint patterns and exports a remediation report
Design and engineering have agreed on a migration plan with rollout milestones and a fallback strategy if regressions are found
notes: Decision: Prefer explicit anchor primitives over bespoke combinations of min/max width and manual frame nesting — simplifies handoff for engineers and reduces variant explosion.

Trade-off: Migration requires touching a large set of instances; to avoid churn we will prioritize surface-critical components first (buttons, tables) and schedule lower-impact atoms for later cycles.
Implementation note: We will add a 'doc-anchoring' tag on migrated components so automation can ignore already-migrated items during subsequent runs.
Engineering asks for a compatibility mapping table so runtime kernels and CSS layout teams can consume naming consistently (attached as CSV in Drive).
qa_steps: Open migrated component in a fresh file, create nested instances simulating dense and wide layouts; verify that resizing parent frames preserves spacing and label truncation behavior.
Run the Figma inspection script and confirm zero 'deprecated-constraint' entries for components in the release branch.
Smoke test: Pull the latest React component storybook for primary controls and visually compare before/after in desktop and mobile viewport snapshots.
Accessibility check: Ensure focus ring and hit-area tokens are not affected by anchor changes (verify token values and interactive states).
publish_curator_checklist: All components in release have a 'doc-anchoring' tag or an approved exception note
Inspection script report attached to the release ticket with zero critical findings
Design reviewer sign-off logged in comments
Engineering compatibility note added to release doc with runtime mapping table
Rollback instructions and affected files list included in release artifacts
